docs/spec/language.md.content: --- spec_id: actql.language status: adopted version: actql/0.1 normative_dependencies: [] --- # ActQL language [Specification index](README.md) This document owns source, types, expressions, operations, nest, effect-intents, canonical-semantics, observable-boundaries. It does not define other owners' wire protocols or a particular Host implementation. Cross-owner links outside the declared dependencies are informative navigation to protocol bindings or conformance evidence; they do not import those documents' requirements. Narrow machine contracts remain authoritative for their explicitly referenced values and envelopes. ## On this page - [Scope and conventions](#scope) - [Source and Program structure](#source-and-program) - [Linear stages](#stages) - [Carriers, values, and types](#values-and-types) - [Inputs and external contracts](#inputs) - [Expressions and predicates](#expressions) - [Operations](#operations) - [Operation inventory](#operation-inventory) - [Relation operations](#relation-operations) - [Event operations (TEA)](#event-operations) - [Graph operations (SGA)](#graph-operations) - [Vector operations (VecA)](#vector-operations) - [Pure lexical ranking: `text_rank`](#text-rank) - [External ranked acquisition: `search_candidates`](#candidate-search) - [Named Results and Effect declarations](#results-and-delivery) - [Checking and canonical planning](#checking-and-planning) - [Structural grammar (normative)](#structural-grammar) - [Complete example (informative)](#complete-example) - [Machine contracts](#machine-contracts) ## Scope and conventions An ActQL Program defines a bounded computation over typed observations, with named Results and optional Effect intents in finite linear stages. The same Program can be executed repeatedly; each execution is managed as a Run. For one Invocation, pure computation yields the same logical Result CIDs. This guarantee does not extend to fresh acquisitions or Effect outcomes ([Capture, execution, and replay](execution.md#capture-and-replay)). The language covers relations, graphs, vectors, event streams, addressable Resources, captured Artifact bytes, bounded external acquisition, and typed provider commands. Arbitrary scripts and raw HTTP are outside the language. AoA supplies the common algebra and canonical fragment representation. Compilation combines validated AoA Fragments and typed boundary barriers into an Executable Plan ([AoA fragments and algebra lowering](#algebra-lowering)). ActQL fixes a Program's observable semantics and leaves physical execution to the Host. Checking establishes static validity and proof obligations under a Check Environment. After binding, planning derives the closed execution envelope, including limits not written in source. A Host MAY fuse, reorder, push down to a Connector, or place computation elsewhere only when the chosen strategy preserves the specified results and ordering, failure and atomicity behavior, observation and data-egress scope, evidence, permission boundaries, and Checkpoints. Sealed Plan identity and approval preservation are specified in [Typed barriers and Plan Documents](#plan-documents); runtime admission is specified in [Checkpoints and Resolutions](execution.md#checkpoints). The Program declares semantic choices and any independent author guards. Contracts supply external-system meaning; checking derives execution facts; the Host supplies current policy and execution ceilings. Concrete observations and continuation state belong to the Run, not to Program source. ### Normative conventions The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **REQUIRED**, **SHALL**, **SHALL NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT**, **RECOMMENDED**, **NOT RECOMMENDED**, **MAY**, and **OPTIONAL** in this document are to be interpreted as described by RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals. Except for examples and text explicitly marked informative, this document is normative. YAML examples, including [Complete example (informative)](#complete-example), illustrate the rules rather than define them. Formal grammars, contract definitions, and semantic tables are normative regardless of their code-block formatting. **Checking** determines whether a Program satisfies the static language rules under a Check Environment. **Binding** supplies declared invocation values. **Planning** produces the canonical bound Executable Plan. These are semantic phases, not command names or requirements on an implementation's internal pass structure. Their results and permitted external access are specified in [Checking and canonical planning](#checking-and-planning); execution is specified in [Run execution](execution.md#effects-and-execution). Planning fixes an execution contract, not an immutable physical strategy. Strategy selection and scheduling may continue during preparation and execution under that contract ([Typed barriers and Plan Documents](#plan-documents)). | Phase | Supplied inputs | Result | External work permitted by this phase | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Checking | Program, Check Environment | Rejection for language violations or the checker's claim boundary, or a valid template with binding/proof obligations | None; evidence is supplied, not fetched | | Binding | Declared parameter and opaque values | Exact typed values, or missing/invalid bindings | No provider observation or Effect | | Planning | Checked Program, all bindings, Check Environment | Canonical bound Plan and execution-support status | None | | Execution | Bound Plan, current authorization, initial captured inputs | Captured observations, Results, receipts, or a recorded failure/pause | Only the admitted Plan boundaries | Initial input capture occurs during each activated stage's preparation, subject to authorization and Checkpoints. Program-wide checking cannot prefetch a later stage's business data ([Run admission and identity](execution.md#run-admission)). Host Discovery ([Host Discovery protocol](protocols/discovery.md#discovery)) explicitly supplies published contracts before checking; optional read collection ([Read collection protocol](protocols/collection.md#collection)) coordinates separate Runs. Neither adds implicit I/O or failure recovery to compilation or pure operations. Checking validity, binding completeness, and Host execution support are distinct judgments. Rejection at a checker's profile-claim boundary does not assert that the Program violates the language, and does not establish its validity. A valid template without bindings is not runnable. A fully checked bound Plan whose execution the Host does not support is `unsupported`, not runnable; neither state grants access to external data. The public status mapping is defined in [Plan Documents and public planning results](protocols/contracts.md#planning-wire). ### Terms The following terms distinguish source, checked meaning, captured computation, and Host lifecycle. Requirements governing their identities and transitions are specified in [Canonical identities](#canonical-identities), [AoA fragments and algebra lowering](#algebra-lowering), [Capture, execution, and replay](execution.md#capture-and-replay), and [Run admission and identity](execution.md#run-admission). - **Generator** — an operation that establishes its output without consuming implicit current; any named additional inputs are still explicit dependencies. - **Delta** — typed graph-value change data bound to exact base, target and structural contract identities; it is neither a capability nor a mutation. - **Coverage** — evidence about the scope and completeness of a captured observation, not a percentage or proof of absence beyond that scope. - **Program** — an `actql/0.1` document describing a bounded computation, published Results, and optional Effect intents. Its semantic content is distinguished from presentation-only Authoring Context. - **Bounded** — each runnable capacity limit has a checked Resolved limit, witnesses, and a defined enforcement boundary; exceeding the ceiling fails the protected work. The applicable limits are specified by the operations and [resolved-limit rules](#resolved-limits). Exact row counts, cost, or duration need not be known before execution; this does not remove their applicable ceilings. - **Resource** — a provider-addressable thing whose identity, kind, authority scope, lifecycle, and version survive any one tabular representation. - **SourceView** — a Connector-owned, versioned typed observation contract over a Resource or resource extent. - **Carrier** — a logical typed value on which the algebra computes: a relation, graph, vector set, or event stream ([Carriers](#carriers)). - **ModelTask** — a versioned contract for bounded structured model acquisition ([Model acquisition: `infer`](#infer)). - **Effect** — explicit intent to change external state. - **Effect Set** — the unordered finite set of Effects declared by one stage and materialized from its Stage Invocation. Set and member semantics are defined in [Effect declarations](#effects). - **Stage Definition** — a stable local stage ID and canonical local semantics, included in the Program's ordered stage descriptors without hashing its parent. - **Unit Definition** — the common Run Graph local definition of an extracted stage: its stable Program-ID/node-ID namespace, Stage Definition, used parameter declarations and incoming producer/import/freshness/gate declarations. It never includes the enclosing Program revision or unrelated stages; see [Local approval dependencies](#local-approval). - **Program checked template** — all stages checked with typed future ports; it is not a collection of fabricated concrete Stage Invocations. - **Stage Invocation** — the semantic identity of one captured stage computation, including its adopted numeric and model observations and imported receipts. - **Program Run** — the common Run Graph execution of a staged Program, retaining its logical request, immutable values, pins and recovery history; not a second orchestration state machine. - **Author guard** — an optional author-declared upper limit that fails protected work when its measured scope exceeds the limit; it does not select the first N items ([Author guards, resolved limits, and Plan facts](#resolved-limits)). - **Program Definition** — the authority-bearing identity combining the Program's authored `id` and canonical semantics, identified by `program_definition_cid` ([Canonical identities](#canonical-identities)). - **Authoring Context** — the nonsemantic metadata sidecar associated with a Program Definition and displayed alongside its checked meaning ([Authoring Context](#authoring-context)). - **Resolved limit** — the checked effective ceiling combining available bounds and guards, with their provenance and enforcement boundary ([Author guards, resolved limits, and Plan facts](#resolved-limits)). - **Executable Plan** — the closed checked envelope of validated AoA Fragments, typed barriers, and their execution constraints and evidence ([AoA fragments and algebra lowering](#algebra-lowering)). ### Common AoA foundation ActQL 0.1 normatively pins the AoA Kernel law-manifest identity, AoA Pipeline IR version, Pipeline law-manifest identity, the reference executable operation-registry identity, the complete target-module contract and its required AoA registry additions, and law `aoa.pipeline.effect-plan.terminal-boundary.v0.1`. These semantic references form the machine-readable `actql-aoa-contract/0.1` artifact, identified by `ACTQL_AOA_CONTRACT_CID`. A conforming ActQL 0.1 compiler MUST report the `ACTQL_AOA_CONTRACT_CID` published by its frozen 0.1 conformance manifest. It MUST NOT silently substitute a newer AoA contract. Every frozen conformance report MUST include the exact value it executed. Package names, registry versions, and source commits are informative reference implementation bindings only. They do not constrain an independent conforming implementation that supplies the same normative semantic identities. The semantic contracts imported by this document are explicitly pinned in [Machine contracts](#machine-contracts). The family-wide [contract index](conformance.md#contract-index) is informative navigation, not an import of every listed protocol. An implementation's internal language, data structures, and compiler pass names do not replace those shared contracts. ### Language boundaries ActQL has no UDF, lambda, custom reducer, user-defined operator registry, inline JavaScript/Python, arbitrary WASM, runtime macro, or `custom_compute` escape hatch. Adding a contract CID around opaque code does not make its purity, bounds, ordering, pushdown, or replay semantics inspectable and MUST NOT be treated as an ActQL operation. Semantics outside ActQL 0.1 or the checker's claimed profiles MUST fail during check with a stable error code. The compiler MUST NOT: - invent an operation; - silently drop an input or field; - change exact computation to approximate computation; - convert event time to processing time; - convert one join kind to another; - return an empty result as a substitute for unsupported behavior. ActQL 0.1 additionally rejects unbounded watch execution, continuous streams, interactive/duplex sessions, arbitrary binary algebra, raw SQL or provider-specific query languages, raw or uncontracted HTTP, ANN as pure VecA, implicit Carrier conversion, cross-provider transactions, Saga orchestration, and natural-language interpretation. Effect composition and its orchestration boundaries are defined in [Effect declarations](#effects). A provider session or long-running operation may be represented as a Resource, bounded incoming observations as events, and outgoing work as a typed command, but its interactive lifecycle remains host application state. The closed vocabulary does not include PageRank, community detection, random walks, PCA, general graph clustering or graph isomorphism. Their addition requires an explicit algorithm, initialization/iteration, numerical and resource contract; they are not rejected on the premise that all such algorithms are inherently nondeterministic. Degree distributions compose degree with group. Arbitrary theta joins, dynamic pivot columns and generic failure-catching remain excluded; interval_join and explicit acquisition coverage do not introduce those broader semantics. Run Graph and HTTP transport are companion contracts, not Program vocabulary ([Artifact and companion contract index (normative)](conformance.md#contract-index)). Proposals for future language extensions follow the separate, informative [extension policy](../design/extension-policy.md). ## Source and Program structure The common Program source model is a closed JSON-model document. [Structural grammar (normative)](#structural-grammar) defines its structural grammar; this chapter defines representation, naming, and authoring context. Explicit frontend profiles can lower other source representations into this same model, followed by ordinary admission and the common checker. ### Source representation ActQL source files SHOULD use the `.aql` extension for YAML, JSON and adopted query representations. The extension identifies the language, not the representation, and does not select a parser. The [Frontend r1 adoption registry](../../spec/frontend/frontend-profile-r1.json) records adopted query/pattern profiles and the withdrawal of the old `AQL / PROGRAM / STAGE / STEP / OP` text surface separately from installed parser support. JSON/YAML Program remains public machine input. A caller selects an installed frontend explicitly; a failure in that frontend does not trigger reinterpretation as another format. Each frontend preserves the closed Program model, explicit steps, semantic array order and the existing checking rules. Profile adoption alone is not runtime conformance evidence. ActQL source MAY be encoded as YAML or JSON. YAML input MUST be restricted to the JSON data model: - object with string keys; - array; - string; - finite number; - boolean; - null. YAML tags, anchors, aliases, merge keys, executable types, non-string mapping keys, non-finite numbers, duplicate keys, and implementation-specific scalar types MUST be rejected. Source text encoding MUST be UTF-8. Object key order MUST NOT affect parsing, lowering, or logical identity. Array order is semantic. Duplicate object keys MUST be rejected before validation. The `actql-source-decoding/0.1` profile uses [YAML 1.2.2 Core scalar resolution](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#103-core-schema), restricted as above, or JSON syntax. Exactly one non-empty object document is required. A single leading UTF-8 BOM is permitted and is not a value; additional documents and invalid UTF-8 are rejected. Numeric tokens decode to binary64 using round-to-nearest, ties-to-even; overflow and negative zero are rejected. Thus YAML `yes`, `on`, and `2026-09-06` are strings, `01` is number 1, and `1e3` is number 1000. JSON does not admit `01` as a number token. Source decoding interprets the selected source syntax's escapes and, for YAML, its scalar folding/chomping. The resulting well-formed Unicode string values are preserved exactly, including CR, LF, CRLF and composed/decomposed sequences. Builder-provided JSON-model strings already are values and receive no second escape interpretation. Object member names use the separate identifier rule, except inside the quoted Effect literal payloads specified below: Unicode 16.0 NFC, then CRLF and lone CR to LF; colliding names are rejected. Identifier-valued members are admitted by their grammar-owned identifier rules, not by normalization of every String. Admission of a purportedly canonical machine artifact rejects noncanonical identifiers or bytes rather than repairing signed or hashed material. A data string need not be NFC or LF-normalized. At a grammar-owned `EffectValue` position, the explicit `{literal: value}` wrapper quotes the complete value subtree. Member names inside that subtree retain their exact decoded Unicode scalar sequences and CR/LF for source and Program identity, including when a later checked target contract is an Object. Exact decoded duplicate keys remain source errors; distinct keys that would collide only after identifier normalization remain distinct source keys there. Program syntax, the `literal` wrapper, Effect names and target-field names retain their existing identifier rules. This exception does not select the payload's type or change any other source position. Contract-directed admission of the payload follows [Effect declarations](#effects). ### Document structure Complete Programs use the stage structure shown below and in the [stage scenarios](../../spec/product-decisions/SCENARIOS.md). Unwrapped pipeline snippets in operation sections describe stage-local bodies. The language version is `actql/0.1`; the pinned Grammar identity identifies the exact grammar. The checker MUST reject root `inputs`, `from`, `steps` or `effects` as invalid top-level members. A missing `stages` fails required-member checking. The compiler MUST NOT invent a stage or execute an implicit repair. ```yaml version: actql/0.1 id: orders.shipped_recent stages: - id: main inputs: orders: carrier: relation schema: id: type: string nullable: false status: type: string nullable: false created_at: type: timestamp nullable: false primary_key: - id from: orders steps: - filter: status = 'shipped' - select: - id - status - created_at - sort: - created_at: desc - id: asc - take: 100 as: recent_shipments results: main: from: recent_shipments fields: - id - status - created_at order_by: - created_at: desc - id: asc results: main: from: stage: main result: main ``` [Structural grammar (normative)](#structural-grammar) defines the closed top-level shape. The following table is an informative summary, not a second grammar: | Key | Required | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `version` | yes | exactly `actql/0.1` | | `id` | yes | stable author-chosen program identifier | | `meta` | no | non-executable authoring metadata | | `params` | no | closed typed runtime value declarations | | `bindings` | no | host-bound opaque invocation value declarations | | `stages` | yes | nonempty finite ordered array of stage definitions | | `results` | yes | explicit exports of closed Stage Results | Unknown top-level keys MUST be rejected. `id` MUST be a non-empty string. It is an authority-bearing definition namespace, not presentation-only provenance and not an AoA step reference. Changing `id` intentionally changes Program Definition, Invocation, Effect Preview, approval, and idempotency identities, while leaving `program_semantics_cid` unchanged. `meta` is non-executable Authoring Context. Its syntax, identity, and review semantics are defined in [Authoring Context](#authoring-context). ### Linear stages Stages are a source and compilation surface, not a second orchestration runtime. They lower to the common finite Run Graph contract. Every Program, including a single-stage Program, uses the explicit `stages` array. A Program has one nonempty finite `stages` array. Each stage has a unique nonempty `id`, `inputs`, `steps`, a `results` map, optional `from`, `effects` and `meta`. Root `params` and `bindings` are declared once. Dataflow, Result and Effect names are stage-local. The root `results` map contains only exports `{from: {stage: StageId, result: ResultName}}`; it performs no computation or projection. A stage may contain a pure dataflow DAG, but the stage list is linear. All stages MUST be checked before Program execution, including future receipt schemas, references, contracts, profiles and bounds. A future producer supplies a typed unbound port, not a fabricated value or Invocation CID. Missing caller values yield `needs_bindings`; a checked Stage Plan awaiting its predecessor is `pending_predecessor`, not missing caller input. Concrete Stage Plans bind every used import and effective parameter before admission; Stage Invocation identity is completed only after its required observations have been captured. Stage inputs additionally accept `{result: {stage, result}}` and `{receipt: {stage, effect}}`. They import an earlier Stage Result or the typed success view of an earlier Effect receipt. Self/forward references, temporary `as` imports, cycles and cross-stage implicit current are rejected. The ordinary input/`as`/multi-output namespace and sole-materialized-input completion apply within each stage. Imports never trigger a provider read. Zero-row imports retain their checked schema. Root exports retain the selected Stage Result's schema, order and policy; re-projection belongs in a stage. Stage order MUST be preserved even without data dependencies. Fresh SourceView reads occur only after that stage activates, never before an earlier Effect. Static contract resolution is not a business read. Within a stage, Effects are an unordered `attempt_all` set; member rows default to `halt`. No member consumes an outcome of its own stage. Later stages may consume explicitly imported receipts or perform fresh reads. Arbitrary workflow branching, loops, recursion, dynamic stage creation and implicit compensation are not admitted; pure `if` and CASE expressions and contract-bounded retry/poll remain distinct. Only a noninitial stage accepts `after: completed|accepted`; omission normalizes to `completed`. It refers to the immediate predecessor, not a selected DAG edge. Activation requires both predecessor success at that level and availability of every import. `accepted` requires every member applied or validly accepted; it never permits failure or unknown. `completed` additionally requires terminal success of the necessary asynchronous operations. A completion-only file Ref still waits for completion under `after: accepted`. Missing finite completion capability is unsupported at check, not an implicitly nullable import. Any failed or partially applied stage MUST prevent normal downstream activation. An unknown outcome waits for reconciliation. A 99/100 success does not silently advance 99 items into the next stage. A cancelled checkpoint does not resume. Successful stages/items are retained, not rolled back or resent on recovery. Independent per-item progression requires explicitly separate Program Runs; it is not a transparent optimization of the stage barrier. Cleanup, compensation and failure notifications are separate explicit recovery Programs. Every local Stage Result is an execution root. Delivery selection cannot skip a stage, Result or Effect. Local artifacts can survive later failure for authorized inspection. A complete graph output index requires every explicit export and truthful flow evidence; complete export coverage is not flow or business success. Program, stage and execution identities follow the canonical envelopes below. Profile support is checked independently of source validity. ### Pipeline names and references `steps` is an ordered array and MAY be empty. `steps: []` is the identity pipeline over the selected input; Result ordering and projection still lower to AoA steps when declared. Each step object MUST contain exactly one operation key plus OPTIONAL `from`, `as`, and `meta` keys, subject to the generator and multi-output exceptions below. An empty step object is invalid. ```yaml - filter: "status = 'open'" from: opportunities as: open_opportunities ``` Here and in operation snippets, an input/step/Result name is local to the enclosing stage. Root Program Results use only the export form in Stages. For an ordinary consuming step, if `from` is omitted it consumes the current step result. The first step consumes the stage-level `from`. If the stage has exactly one input, the stage-level `from` MAY be omitted and that input is selected deterministically. For these selection rules, count only materialized inputs, not search-template bindings classified under Inputs and external contracts. A template name is not a valid current Carrier, even when it is the only declared input name. If more than one input exists and stage-level `from` is omitted, an ordinary consuming step before any explicit current selection MUST be rejected. A compiler MUST NOT select an input by declaration order. Generators `values`, `time_series`, `calendar_series` and `mean_graphs` reject step-level `from`, require `as`, and set the current result to their output. They consume only the explicitly named additional inputs, if any. Thus an empty inputs map is legal when every dataflow root is generated. Stage-level `from` is absent with zero inputs. With multiple inputs, a generator or an explicit step `from` can establish the current result without a stage-level `from`. `search_candidates` instead binds the two names in its outputs object, rejects `as`, and leaves the current result unchanged. References to these names have the same uniqueness, scope and no-forward-reference rules as as. An authored dataflow binding is an input name, a single-output step's `as`, or an explicitly named multi-output port. Search preserves the current value from before the step, even when its query input uses an explicit `from`. If current was unset it remains unset. Both output names are registered together; neither output order nor explicit query selection updates current. `as` binds a dataflow name for later reuse. All authored dataflow names MUST be non-empty strings. Inputs, `as` names and explicit multi-output names share one dataflow namespace and MUST be unique within it. Result names form a separate publication namespace: `from: name` resolves in the dataflow namespace, while `from: {result: name}` resolves in the publication namespace. A Result MAY therefore reuse a dataflow name. Authors SHOULD NOT reuse one, because a review reader would see the same token denote two objects. Authors SHOULD use `as` for branches, later reuse, or Result publication; generated names are used for ordinary linear steps. Name resolution has the following closed scopes: | Position | Available names | | --- | --- | | Top-level `from` | Declared materialized inputs only; no search templates | | Step `from` and additional Carrier inputs | Materialized inputs and preceding authored Carrier bindings; search.source alone accepts a template binding | | Result `from` | All authored Carrier bindings in the completed pipeline; no templates | | Effect `from` | `{result: name}` in the publication namespace only | Forward references, self-references, cycles, duplicate bindings, and unavailable names MUST fail during check. Compiler-generated names are not author-visible bindings. Join and other multi-input operations name their additional inputs inside the operation. An unavailable or Carrier-incompatible name MUST fail during check. ### Field names and nested paths An `AuthoredFieldName` is a flat NFC string containing at least one non-whitespace character. This rule applies to relation/graph/event/vector fields and recursively to object properties. Here whitespace is the union of ECMAScript 2025 [WhiteSpace and LineTerminator](https://tc39.es/ecma262/2025/multipage/ecmascript-language-lexical-grammar.html#sec-white-space): U+0009–U+000D, U+0020, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000–U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, and U+FEFF. Authored schema fields MUST NOT contain `.`, equal `__cid`, or begin with the reserved `__actql_` prefix. Generated semantic fields such as `edge_id`, `window_start_ms`, `session_id`, and score/identity restorations are checked for collision before lowering. A compiler MUST NOT reinterpret a user field as join provenance or an internal carrier field. Implementations MUST permit line breaks within field names; source NFC/LF normalization and quoted or escaped representations apply as for other strings. `GeneratedFieldName` denotes a field introduced by a specified operation; it is not permission for authors to declare reserved internal fields. `ProvenanceQualifiedFieldReference` is the explicit `left.name` or `right.name` reference to a join operand ([join](#join)), not an authored field. Subsequent property access is a distinct expression node ([Typed access](#typed-access)). A raw qualified join output requires a flat projection before another join; recursive join provenance is not inferred from a chain of dots. A flat field name may hold a closed nested `object` or `array` value. Nested values do not create dotted field names. Typed expression access is specified in [Typed access](#typed-access); `json_pick` remains the explicit relational form: ```yaml - json_pick: column: payload path: [customer, id] output: customer_id ``` > **Note (informative):** `customer.id` selects property `id` of field `customer`; > it cannot name a flat field containing a dot. Before ActQL checking, a Connector adapter MUST map every provider-specific source-field selector into a declared flat canonical ActQL field name. This rule governs field names, not value shape: a declared field may still contain a closed nested value. ### Authoring Context `meta` provides author-supplied annotations for presentation and review. It MAY appear on the Program, a Stage, an Input (including a Result/receipt import), a Parameter or Binding declaration, a Step, a Result, or an Effect. It MUST NOT appear inside expressions, predicates, value contracts, or operation bodies. Short-form inputs use their object form to carry annotations. `Meta` is a non-empty JSON object with service-defined content. Top-level keys beginning with `actql_` are reserved and MUST be rejected in 0.1. Its complete content uses the AoA Kernel canonical JSON contract ([Canonical identities](#canonical-identities)); non-finite numbers, negative zero, and unpaired UTF-16 surrogates MUST be rejected. Metadata is nonsemantic authoring context. It MUST NOT change computation, authority, egress, bounds, optimization, Effect Preview identity, or semantic Program, Executable Plan, Invocation, or idempotency identity. It MUST NOT be copied into a model request, Connector request, Effect payload, or provider prompt. Except for validating metadata itself, Hosts MUST NOT use metadata as a structured input to execution admission or policy, permissions, approval routing, Checkpoint requirements, or Resolution validation. A Host MAY impose metadata capacity or content restrictions, but MUST reject violations at intake with a stable diagnostic code rather than silently truncating or rewriting metadata. An Effect review projection MUST bind both the semantic `effect_preview_cid` and the exact `authoring_context_cid` presented to the reviewer. Metadata MUST be identified as author-supplied and separated from verified authority and approval status. A projection MAY present a CID reference to the canonical metadata instead of rendering its contents; the reference remains subject to the applicable access and redaction policy. Changing only metadata therefore does not rebuild the Effect Preview, but it does require a new review projection and approval attestation. Natural-language metadata MUST NOT satisfy a missing structured semantic choice. ## Carriers, values, and types Carriers describe collections on which the algebra operates. Field contracts describe the values carried by those collections; they are shared by local schemas, external Contracts, expressions, and Results. ### Carriers The graph structural contract has the closed canonical body `{version: "actql-graph-contract/0.1", domain, node_definitions, edge_definitions, identity_law_cid, value_law_cid}`. Each definition retains its name, nonempty ordered key contracts, matching ordered `key_columns`, complete property contracts and static label-to-property sets. Edge definitions additionally name their source and target node definitions. Element identity is the admitted definition domain, definition name and complete typed key, not an endpoint tuple. Independently keyed parallel edges are retained. Property types and shared label property sets obey the graph-wide rules in [Graph construction](#graph-construction). `graph_contract_cid` is the ordinary ActQL CID of exactly this body, without a self-CID member. `key_columns` binds each retained constructor key-column name to its component position and type; an anonymous structural definition uses null entries at every position, never a partially named tuple. Snapshot reload retains this mapping without consulting a catalog. Property-map enumeration, observations, graph contents, row counts, policy and provider locators are not contract members. The retired `actql-graph-contract/0.1` body is not an alternate Graph profile: current admission rejects it without conversion. Historical bytes and evidence retain their original identity, but do not provide current execution support. Operations not connected to this keyed representation must reject explicitly; their old tuple-based implementations are not a fallback. For the 0.1 contract, both graph law CID members MUST equal `graph_law_manifest_cid` in the owned operation-contract inventory. That pin resolves `actql-graph-laws/0.1`, maintained inside ActQL, which contains the semantic identity and typed value equality laws together. Computing a structural contract CID proves neither snapshot admission nor base/target content identity. ActQL source uses four public Carrier names: ```text relation graph vectors events ``` These map directly to the AoA sorts `relation`, `graph`, `vector_set`, and `event_stream`. Every materialized input and every step result has exactly one ActQL Carrier. Conversions are legal only through the deterministic semantic expansions defined in this specification. A compiler MUST NOT reinterpret a value as another Carrier. Relations contain ordered rows with string-named fields. Graph, event-stream, and vector carrier representations are AoA-defined; ActQL restores authored semantic identity field names when returning to relations, except operations with fixed result roles such as `nearest`'s `query_id` / `candidate_id` ([Vector operations (VecA)](#vector-operations)). Physical enumerability, a proven stable total order, and candidate-key evidence are different properties. A **candidate key** is a non-null field tuple proven unique; candidate keys form a set of independent witnesses. An **ordering witness** proves the logical row sequence used by order-sensitive operations. Provider arrival order alone proves neither. A **complete schema** supplies every field name and recursive value contract; knowing some names is not completeness. ### Closed value contracts The closed value type names are `string`, `number`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `timestamp`, `date`, `json`, `object`, `array`, `vector`, `resource_ref`, and `artifact_ref`. The primitive value domains are: | Type | Value domain | | --- | --- | | `string` | Well-formed Unicode scalar sequences, preserved without implicit normalization or line-break conversion. | | `number` | Finite IEEE-754 binary64; negative zero is invalid in canonical source. | | `boolean` | `true` or `false`. | | `decimal` | Precision, scale, and exact base-10 coefficient ([Exact decimal values](#decimal-values)). | | `timestamp` | Canonical UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`; offsets and leap-second spellings are invalid. | | `date` | Canonical `YYYY-MM-DD`; distinct from a timestamp. | `json` provides no recursive static field evidence. `object` and `array` carry the recursive contracts described below; `vector` carries fixed dimensions and the 0.1 f32 element law. Opaque reference values are defined in [Opaque reference values](#opaque-references). Arithmetic, conversion, and null propagation are specified in [Expressions and predicates](#expressions). `resource_ref` and `artifact_ref` additionally declare `resource_kind` or optional `media_type` and require issuer evidence as specified in [Opaque reference values](#opaque-references). Every field contract, including an array element contract or object property contract, MUST declare `nullable`. `array` contracts MUST declare `items`; `object` contracts MUST declare `fields`. These members contain recursive field contracts and are legal only for their respective types. Values without declared internal structure use `json`. For `json_pick` on a typed object, a referenced path MUST be present in the complete recursive contract. When `schema` is present, it is complete: runtime rows MUST have exactly that field set and every value, nested array element, and declared object property MUST satisfy the declared type/nullability. `nullable: true` permits a present value to be `null`; it does not make the field or property optional. Relation column presence is separate from these ordinary object value rules. A finite complete Relation schema MAY declare a column conditional: an absent row key is omission, not an explicit NULL. Required columns MUST occur in every row; every present cell MUST satisfy its declared value type and nullability. The existence guarantee MUST participate in schema identity and retained schema storage. Row content identity MUST distinguish omitted keys from explicit NULL, without including physical presence bitmap/layout choices. In the initial presence profile, ordinary references and public Result columns MUST be schema-guaranteed present. Conditional references MUST fail during checking; sample values, an empty Relation and `IS NOT NULL` do not prove presence. Projection of guaranteed columns and filter/derive expressions that reference only guaranteed columns, Required-key sort, proven-order take and keyed DISTINCT over guaranteed columns, complete-row DISTINCT and GROUP over guaranteed references are supported. Structural DROP MAY remove columns from a conditional schema without reading retained values; it MUST preserve the retained columns' contracts, presence, order and row correspondence, and admit and charge the complete input, including removed columns. It does not make retained Conditional fields ordinary references. Filter MUST preserve the exact input schema, ordered surviving rows and each cell's presence; it MUST admit and charge all input rows before evaluating the predicate, including rejected rows. All syntactic references require presence, including unevaluated branches. Other consumers of a conditional schema remain explicitly unsupported until their preservation or refinement rules are implemented; they MUST NOT fill omission with NULL or silently drop presence. This does not make ordinary object properties optional. Derive MUST preserve untouched fields' presence, values and row correspondence through execution, retention and reload, without filling omission with NULL. A computed derive binding MUST be Required with its checked type and nullable contract; ordered replacement refers to the new binding rather than proving the replaced input column present. Derive MUST reject every reference to an unguaranteed input column during checking, including unevaluated branches; references to a proven earlier binding in ordered derive retain the existing value-version semantics. Sort and take on conditional Relation inputs MUST preserve the input schema, each selected row's values and presence, and the existing canonical content identity rules through retention and reload. Authored sort keys MUST be schema-guaranteed present, while ordering completion, take determinacy, complete input admission and resource accounting retain their existing obligations; neither observed samples nor an empty result establish order or presence. Keyed DISTINCT on conditional Relation inputs MUST project only its specified, schema-guaranteed columns before deduplication, preserving their checked value types and nullability and the existing first-occurrence ordering. Unspecified conditional columns MUST NOT survive the projection or participate in equality. The complete sparse input MUST still be admitted and charged, including omitted cells' presence slots and values not selected for output. An unguaranteed key MUST fail during checking. Complete-row `distinct: true` on conditional Relation inputs MUST preserve the input schema, values and presence through deduplication, retention and reload. Equality MUST include presence at every column: omitted and explicitly NULL cells are different, and unselected-key projection is not complete-row equality. The entire input MUST be admitted and charged, including duplicate rows and omission slots. Existing first-occurrence ordering and type-specific equality remain in force; deduplication does not make Conditional columns ordinarily referenceable or publishable and does not establish a new stable-order proof. GROUP on conditional Relation inputs MUST require schema-guaranteed presence for every group key and every reference in aggregate arguments, filters and aggregate-local ordering, including syntactically present unevaluated branches. The complete sparse input MUST be admitted and charged before aggregation, without reading absent unreferenced cells as NULL or omitting their presence storage from resource accounting. The aggregate result MUST retain the existing GROUP output schema, types, nullability, empty-input behavior and ordering through retention and reload; unselected input columns do not survive grouping. Both authored and checked object contracts MUST permit `fields: {}`. This closed contract admits only the empty object, plus `null` when `nullable: true`. An empty array retains its declared item contract; its contents do not infer `json` or change nullability. `nest` ([nest](#nest)) derives that contract from the selected child schema, with a non-null array and non-null object items. The author-facing field contract contains only semantic choices. An authored object contract omits `additional_properties`; the compiler inserts the sole 0.1 machine meaning `additional_properties: false`. An authored vector contract declares positive `dimensions` and omits `element_type`; the compiler inserts the sole 0.1 machine meaning `element_type: f32`. These fixed machine fields appear in checked Plan and protocol contracts but are not authoring vocabulary. The author and checked contracts are separate closed grammars. Every row below also has `type` and required `nullable`; `?` marks an optional member. | Type | Other author members | Checked expansion or evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | `string` | none | optional `min_length`, `max_codepoints`, `max_utf8_bytes` from admitted evidence | | `number`, `boolean`, `timestamp`, `date`, `json` | none | unchanged | | `decimal` | `precision`, `scale` | unchanged; [Exact decimal values](#decimal-values) ranges | | `array` | `items: AuthorValueContract`, `max_items?` | recursive checked `items`; bound unchanged | | `object` | `fields: {AuthoredFieldName: AuthorValueContract}` | recursive checked fields; `additional_properties: false` | | `vector` | `dimensions` | `element_type: f32` | | `resource_ref` | `resource_kind` | unchanged | | `artifact_ref` | `media_type?` | unchanged | `AuthorValueContract` is exactly the author column; `CheckedValueContract` is its recursive expansion plus only the checked members listed above. Unknown or wrong-type members are rejected. Array `max_items` is a non-negative safe integer, including zero; it constrains admitted values, unlike an operation guard over measured work ([Author guards, resolved limits, and Plan facts](#resolved-limits)). Checked string extents are non-negative safe integers and do not become author syntax. `min_length` and `max_codepoints` count Unicode scalar values in the retained string; `max_utf8_bytes` counts that value's UTF-8 bytes before JSON escaping. Neither counts grapheme clusters or UTF-16 code units. Type equality and compatibility use the following common relations: - `TypeEqual(A,B)` compares complete canonical checked contracts recursively, including nullability, bounds, decimal precision/scale, vector dimensions, reference kind/media type, and object field sets. Object key order is irrelevant. - `Assignable(A,B)` means every value permitted by A satisfies B. Non-null may flow to nullable, but not conversely. Base types match without coercion; decimal precision/scale, vector dimensions, and ResourceKind must match. Objects have exactly the same field set with recursively assignable values; arrays have assignable items. An actual upper bound cannot exceed an expected bound, and an actual lower bound cannot be smaller. Missing bounds prove no restriction. An unspecified expected Artifact media type admits any media type; a specified type requires that exact type to be proven. - `JoinNullability(A,B)` requires the same recursive base structure and the exact decimal/vector/ResourceKind parameters. It takes nullable OR at each position and the least restrictive common value bounds. Different Artifact media types join to an unspecified media type. Other base-type differences have no join. `json` is not an implicit supertype of typed objects or references. `append`, conditional result branches, `coalesce`, and array construction use this common join. SourceView request and Command argument checking use assignability. A literal null acquires a nullable form of the other branch's known type; all-null expressions alone provide no non-null type evidence. An explicit cast of null supplies its target type with `nullable: true`. An immediate fixed signature also supplies a literal NULL's type when its argument domain is unique: `len(NULL)` uses nullable string, `concat(NULL,NULL)` uses string arguments, and `NULL IS TRUE` and `CASE WHEN NULL THEN 1 ELSE 2 END` use a nullable boolean condition. An overloaded argument without a unique domain supplies no type; two untyped NULL operands of `IS DISTINCT FROM` still require independent type evidence. For `quantize` and `decimal_divide`, implementations MUST NOT use the output precision and scale to supply an input type: the decimal input domain has no unique precision/scale, and the divisor domain also permits `number`. Bare literal NULL operands remain unresolved; an explicit cast such as `CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(8,2))` supplies the missing input type. Already-typed nullable operands still propagate null. An empty array obtains its item type from an explicit `empty_array.items` contract or the unique common item type of independently typed peers in an `if`/`case`, `coalesce`, or array constructor. A schema-typed array with `max_items: 0` and an explicitly typed empty array both supply evidence. Resolution is recursive, ignores only untyped NULL and untyped `[]` as type evidence, and fails if no unique type remains. It never searches arbitrary downstream consumers. The empty array itself is non-null with `max_items: 0`; peer nullability is not copied to it. An unresolved field may acquire its type from one explicitly mapped nullable ModelTask input. Outside these explicit type, local signature and peer rules, no other consumer context supplies an unresolved null type in 0.1; absence of a unique type fails with `ACTQL_E_NULL_TYPE_UNRESOLVED`. An operation may impose stricter preconditions, but not a different coercion. Expression-specific nullability, such as `coalesce` being non-null when an argument is proven non-null, is refined by [Expressions and predicates](#expressions) after this structural join. `KeyComparable(A,B)` compares non-null value domains, not entire contracts. Nullability and value-size bounds may differ; each input still satisfies its own contract, and the operation's null policy governs null keys. Base types must match without coercion. Decimal precision/scale may differ: decimal keys compare by exact numeric value under [Exact decimal values](#decimal-values). ResourceKind must match; ArtifactRef media restrictions do not change reference equality. Scalar and reference domains are comparable under these rules; object, array, json, and vector keys are not admitted. Join-key compatibility uses this relation, not `TypeEqual`. For `json_pick` through a closed object, result nullability is the OR of the leaf's nullability and every traversed parent's nullability. A null parent returns null; an absent declared property violates the input contract. Parameter declarations reuse the recursive value domains with the parameter-specific default and nullability rules in [Parameters and binding](#parameters). `date` and `timestamp` use the proleptic Gregorian calendar with years 0000 through 9999 and valid month/day combinations. Timestamps require hours 00–23, minutes/seconds 00–59, and exactly three fractional digits in UTC. Leap seconds and out-of-range dates fail. These value rules apply without the optional text-time profile, which only adds transformations over the domain. ### Exact decimal values Decimal follows the AoA RelA exact-decimal contract. The closed type is `{type: decimal, precision: P, scale: S, nullable: boolean}`, with integer `1 <= P <= 38` and `0 <= S <= P`. Its exact value is `coefficient × 10^(-S)`. The machine coefficient is a base-10 integer string matching `0|-?[1-9][0-9]*`, with at most P digits excluding the sign; leading zeros, a leading `+`, and negative zero are invalid. Typed value identity is domain-separated from string identity and includes the decimal contract version, P, S, and coefficient. Each declared type has exactly one canonical spelling per value. Thus `19.90` at scale 2 and `19.900` at scale 3 compare numerically equal but have different types and typed value identities. Arithmetic and conversion rules are defined in [Decimal expressions](#decimal-expressions). Decimal comparison, including join-key equality, compares the exact values `coefficient × 10^(-S)` without binary64 conversion or rounding. Equivalently, compare integer coefficients aligned to the greater scale; this comparison introduces no precision-38 intermediate-value restriction. Different precision or scale does not prevent comparison or an equal-key match. Hash-based joins use the same numeric equality, not typed value CID equality. This does not change either operand's type, canonical spelling, or typed value identity; changing a stored decimal's precision/scale still requires explicit conversion. Canonical JSON, JSONL, and CSV serialization uses fixed-scale decimal text: exactly S fractional digits, no exponent or leading `+`, and no redundant integer leading zeros. When S is zero, the decimal point is omitted. JSON and JSONL encode this text as a string; declared decimal JSON inputs use that same canonical spelling. A coefficient outside the declared precision fails rather than being rounded or truncated. ### Opaque reference values Two opaque scalar types cross carrier boundaries: - `resource_ref` is a projected Resource identity. It contains a provider namespace plus content identities for provider identity, authority scope, Resource boundary, and the complete reference. It contains no native provider locator, view, connector version, observation time, etag, or schema evidence. - `artifact_ref` identifies captured bytes and carries content CID, media type, bounded byte count/range, storage scope, truncation, sensitivity, capture authority, and optional source ResourceRef/version evidence. ResourceRef equality is equality of `identity_cid`, scoped by provider namespace, ResourceKind, provider identity, authority scope, and boundary. Connection names and authentication revisions do not determine that identity. ArtifactRef equality is equality of `artifact_ref_cid`, including store, scope, retention, and policy; equal `content_cid` values establish byte identity only. SourceView and serialization output contracts may expose `content_cid` as a separate field. Reference equality MUST be consistent across predicates, joins, grouping, distinct, and uniqueness checks, independently of acquisition or in-memory object identity. Within each reference type, `eq`/`neq` use that equality. References are scalar keys for equality-based operations. For specification-defined canonical identity ordering and deterministic compiler completion, use AoA code-unit order of `identity_cid` for ResourceRefs or `artifact_ref_cid` for ArtifactRefs. This includes canonical group/partition enumeration and request-key ordering where the operation already admits reference keys; it does not expand any operation's admitted key or Carrier types. Machine-only means not author-selectable as a reference value order, not unobservable: the resulting canonical order remains part of observable semantics. Author-order restrictions and their validation boundaries are defined in [Lexical and ordering rules](#ordering). Only a Connector host may issue a `resource_ref`. An `artifact_ref` may be issued only by a Connector capture or an authorized content-addressed Artifact Store derivation. Both issuers bind typed issuer evidence; the public protocol exports validators, not an author-accessible issuer. A reference grants no authority. Host-accepted bindings and Artifact or Result inputs MUST revalidate issuer evidence and current usage authorization; authored JSON alone cannot establish a valid reference. References serialize as tagged canonical JSON objects, but their internals MUST NOT be inspected or modified by expressions or `json_pick`. An operation requiring a ResourceRef MUST receive it explicitly; hidden execution lineage MUST NOT restore a projected-away reference or supply an implicit write target. Mapping-based Effect selectors remain valid ([Effect declarations](#effects)). Binary bytes and base64 are not embedded into ordinary AoA JSON values, and image/audio-specific carriers do not exist. ### Lexical and ordering rules `AuthorOrderable` comprises `string`, `number`, `decimal`, `boolean`, `timestamp`, and `date`. `CanonicalOrderable` comprises those types plus `resource_ref` and `artifact_ref`. These are specification classifications, not source syntax. A portable order is the specified total order over non-null values of a `CanonicalOrderable` type: numeric order for `number` and `decimal`, `false < true` for `boolean`, chronological order for `timestamp` and `date`, the string order below, and reference identity order ([Opaque reference values](#opaque-references)). `object`, `array`, `json`, and `vector` have no portable order. Null placement follows the operation's rules; null does not acquire a value order. Every authored ordering key, ordered-comparison operand, and `min`/`max` input MUST be `AuthorOrderable`, regardless of operation or field spelling. This includes ranking and explicit tie-break keys, but not equality-based partition, grouping, correlation, or uniqueness keys. Reference identity order is available only for specification-defined canonical identity ordering and deterministic compiler completion ([Opaque reference values](#opaque-references)). Statically invalid order domains MUST be rejected during check. Where an existing rule permits deferred type validation, the Plan MUST retain the `AuthorOrderable` obligation and the runtime input boundary MUST validate it before evaluating the ordering operation. This rule permits no new deferral and never authorizes reference ordering. Every lexicographic ordering in this specification uses UTF-16 code-unit order on the admitted values. String data is not normalized for comparison; identifier names retain their separate NFC/LF admission contract. Locale collation and Unicode code-point order are not permitted alternatives. Connector references are non-empty UTF-8 strings whose normalized spelling is identity-bearing. Author-facing Mapping Contract references use the typed-qualified closed ASCII grammar in [Mapping contracts](protocols/contracts.md#mapping-contracts). They are not inferred from the surrounding field and do not change spelling during compilation. A compiler does not perform provider-specific case folding. Duration tokens have lexical form `[0-9]+(ms|s|m|h|d)`, are ASCII case-insensitive at authoring, and canonicalize to positive safe integer milliseconds. Negative zero and non-finite numbers are invalid before identity computation. ## Inputs and external contracts An input referenced as `search_candidates.source` declares an acquisition template, not a captured Relation. Check classifies that binding before input selection: it resolves the SourceView and static request without dispatch, and excludes it from initial capture and implicit sole-input selection. All references to that binding are template references from search steps; using it as top-level/step `from`, a local operation operand or Result input fails check, including mixed template/Relation use in one Program. Multiple search steps may reuse the template. An independent snapshot requires a separate input binding with its own complete request and capture evidence. Dynamic request roles are supplied only by each search step; static and dynamic roles together match the exact request contract. Template resolution does not grant provider access, create rows, or establish observation completeness. Parameter and opaque binding values are declared and supplied under [Parameters and binding](#parameters); they are distinct from the external contracts selected by an input. The external and computational models are orthogonal: ```text Resource -> SourceView ---------------------> Carrier Relation -> ModelTask infer acquisition ----> Relation Relation -> keyed SourceView join acquisition -> Relation Relation -> Artifact serialization ---------> Relation Relation -> typed external SourceView join -> Relation Carrier -> AoA algebra -> Effect Plan -> Receipt ``` Resource, SourceView, Carrier, and Effect are defined in [Terms](#terms). SourceView, ModelTask, and Artifact serialization contracts are versioned barrier contracts, not intermediate languages. External inference and the acquisition selected for an external join are not AoA operations or business-state mutation Effects. Relation serialization is an explicit Artifact barrier rather than a hidden output-side post-processing pass. ### Input duplicate normalization Materialized relation inputs accept `duplicates: reject` or `duplicates: {first_by_order: {order_by: [OrderKey, ...]}}`; omission normalizes to `reject`. The array is nonempty and uses declared raw fields and the ordinary OrderKey grammar. The bare string `first_by_order` is invalid. First-by-order selects the first complete row per declared primary-key tuple using an independently admitted total order. The duplicated key itself, provider arrival order or an invented payload-CID tie-break is not that proof. Without it checking fails; an unkeyed raw input followed by explicit `dedupe_rows` is a separate business-selection path. Admission MUST decode and normalize optional provider fields, then validate all raw rows' known fields, types, nullability and non-null key components before selection. A discarded malformed row cannot be hidden. Raw rows/bytes and normalized rows/bytes have separate limits. Non-null uniqueness is proved only on the selected output. Evidence binds the raw artifact, policy, order witness, normalized artifact and excluded count. Raw capture cursor and coverage are unchanged. An authoritative SourceView uniqueness violation remains a contract failure, not something an author can repair with `first_by_order` or a local schema override. ### Local typed inputs A local input MAY use the short form: ```yaml inputs: rows: relation graph: graph events: events embeddings: vectors ``` or the object form: ```yaml inputs: rows: carrier: relation expected_columns: [id, status] ``` An optional inline `schema` supplies the closed field contracts defined in [Closed value contracts](#value-contracts): ```yaml inputs: orders: carrier: relation schema: id: {type: string, nullable: false} amount: {type: number, nullable: true} occurred_at: {type: timestamp, nullable: false} items: type: array nullable: false items: type: object nullable: false fields: sku: {type: string, nullable: false} quantity: {type: number, nullable: false} primary_key: [id] ``` `primary_key`, when present, is a non-empty field list. When a complete schema is available, every component MUST exist in it, have a scalar or reference type ([Opaque reference values](#opaque-references)), and declare `nullable: false`. At the runtime input boundary, every component MUST be present, non-null, and a scalar or reference value, and, after the explicitly admitted input duplicate normalization, the complete tuple MUST be unique by canonical-value equality, including when static type evidence is unavailable. Reference components use the equality defined in [Opaque reference values](#opaque-references). The Host may supply schema evidence under [Check Environment and source evidence](protocols/contracts.md#check-environment) without an authored `schema`. Such evidence MUST satisfy any explicit input assertions. `schema_ref` is not an input field; unresolved descriptive labels belong in `meta` ([Authoring Context](#authoring-context)). `carrier` is REQUIRED for an opaque local input. `expected_columns` is OPTIONAL but, when present, MUST be a duplicate-free array of non-empty field names. Runtime bindings MUST be checked against it before computation. It requires those columns to be present but permits additional columns and specifies neither column order nor value types. A compiler MUST NOT infer a complete field set from `expected_columns` alone. When `schema` is also present, every expected column MUST belong to that schema. Check reports one of three evidence levels rather than rejecting every partially described relation: `typed` for a resolved complete schema, `columns_only` for known column names without a complete typed schema, and `unknown` when neither is available. Static evidence checking MUST NOT reject an operation solely because evidence unrelated to its required proofs is absent. This rule does not exempt language violations, authorization denials, or runtime failures. A required proof must be established during check unless the operation's existing rules permit a deferred validation obligation; such an obligation is retained in the Plan and discharged at its specified runtime boundary. These evidence levels introduce no additional permission to defer validation. Known field names, field-set completeness, recursive type evidence, candidate keys, and ordering witnesses are independent evidence axes. `columns_only` may describe a subset or a complete set of names; the complete set must have separate evidence. The three levels above summarize type knowledge, not all five axes. ### Connector SourceViews A connector input names a Host-published Connector instance (`connector`), a Resource within it (`resource`), and an observation of that Resource (`view`). The instance selector identifies a Catalog entry, not a Connector implementation name or connection revision ([Resource identity contract](#resource-identity-contract)). For example, if the admitted Catalog exposes only the `records` SourceView for `Opportunity`: ```yaml inputs: opportunities: connector: crm/main resource: Opportunity from: opportunities steps: - select: [id, account_id, stage, amount] - filter: "stage NOT IN ('ClosedWon', 'ClosedLost')" ``` `connector` and `resource` are required. When `view` is omitted, Check MUST resolve it from all SourceViews for that exact pair in the admitted Catalog: zero views is rejected as unresolved; one is completed under `actql.source.sole-view-completion`; more than one is rejected with `ACTQL_E_SOURCE_VIEW_AMBIGUOUS` and the candidate list. Resolution MUST NOT filter candidates by current execution permissions, request compatibility, or downstream expressions. An explicitly selected SourceView MUST match the full `(connector, resource, view)` selector, including when a contract CID is pinned. Check does not synthesize a SourceView, implicitly select `records`, or fall back across Resources. Catalog publication is governed by [Connector Catalog and lock](protocols/contracts.md#catalog-and-lock). SourceView resolution MUST bind the concrete Resource using its admitted output data-policy `source_ref`, exactly `"connector://" + connector_id + "/" + resource + "#" + view_id`, with nonempty `resource`; `resource_kind` is a type, not that address. This is literal string construction, not URL parsing: the known `connector_id` prefix and `view_id` suffix delimit the Resource. Percent escapes, slashes and fragment characters inside the Resource remain literal. Authored selectors use their source-normalized strings exactly, with no URI-prefix removal, slash trimming, percent decoding or case folding. Different Resources may expose the same kind and view name. Before resolving inputs, Check MUST reject every supplied SourceView whose policy source reference does not have that exact prefix, nonempty Resource and suffix, and reject duplicate `(connector_id, resource, view_id)` selectors, even across different kinds or versions and even when unused. This check follows policy-reference admission; Catalog integrity alone does not establish Resource selector uniqueness. Ambiguous candidate names are reported in UTF-16 order. The resolved Plan MUST identify the SourceView and bind its contract CID. A Catalog change requires rechecking against the new Catalog; it MUST NOT retarget a sealed Plan. Completion is recorded in the normalization journal ([Deterministic completion](#completion)), not required as a rewrite of the authored Program. The SourceView contract determines acquisition semantics, read authority, output Carrier/schema/facts, ResourceRef issuance, read modes, checkpoint/delivery contract, and pushdown capabilities. Authors MUST NOT repeat the output Carrier. A relation SourceView lowers directly to an AoA relation source; SourceView resolution is not another IR. Catalog discovery MUST expose each SourceView's name, request contract, acquisition kind, authority, observation classification, output Carrier/schema, modes, and contract CID, including any extraction contract. Human-readable discovery MUST present these facts rather than names alone. Authors and generators select SourceViews from this evidence, not by inferring meaning from their names. Acquisition review projections MUST include the SourceView classification and contract identities reported by the Plan summary ([Diagnostic documents](protocols/contracts.md#diagnostic-documents)), subject to redaction. `request` is validated against the resolved SourceView `request_schema`. It may contain literals, typed scalar parameters, or an explicit `{$binding: name}`. Opaque invocation bindings are declared separately from scalar parameters: ```yaml bindings: target_file: type: resource_ref resource_kind: google_drive.file inputs: file: connector: google_drive/main resource: drive_file view: content request: resource_ref: {$binding: target_file} max_bytes: 262144 require_full: false ``` Each field of an authored static `request` is one whole-value slot. An exact singleton `{$param: name}` or `{$binding: name}` at that slot denotes the named declaration; other slot values are literal JSON. Request decoding MUST NOT descend into literal values to discover or substitute references. In particular, nested parameter-shaped or binding-shaped business objects are data, and a `literal` key does not introduce an additional request quotation operator. The resolved request contract still determines each slot's admissible type and whether all required static and correlation roles are covered. The host supplies the opaque binding at invocation. Its declaration and request position belong to Program identity; the concrete binding belongs to Invocation identity and `resolved_request_cid` source evidence. Bindings MUST be used only inside SourceView requests. A binding MUST NOT create a ResourceRef or ArtifactRef. The host invocation contract MUST expose each declaration name and its `resource_kind` or media-type constraint separately from the opaque values artifact. Authors MUST NOT inspect that artifact to discover keys, and authoring tooling or compiler MUST NOT guess a missing binding name. Without all declared opaque bindings, checking establishes only a template proof. An executable Plan requires every binding, validated for presence, kind, and request compatibility ([Parameters and binding](#parameters)). Execution MUST use those bound values. The public planning result MUST redact opaque values and resolved requests, reporting only declaration names, constraints, and binding status. Ordinary SourceView requests are static: they may use literals, parameters, and Host bindings. Data-dependent SourceView acquisition uses the checked external-join lowering in [External SourceView joins](#external-joins), or [search_candidates](#candidate-search) for ranked candidate retrieval. A finite left key/query set drives one pinned SourceView access path, with the distinct completeness requirements of each operation. Programs cannot author a general fetch/follow DAG or row-driven acquisition loop. Every field declared by a complete request contract is present in the resolved request object. `nullable: true` permits the value `null`; it does not permit the field to be absent. A Connector MUST bind every declared request field to one typed planning/execution consumer. Declaring a field and then ignoring it is a contract error. Every resolved SourceView is a canonical `actql.source_view/0.1` contract with: ```text connector_id, connector_version, resource_kind, view_id, view_version, acquisition {kind, authority, request_schema, modes, default_mode, optional correlation {request_fields, response_fields, identity, cardinality}, optional batching}, observation {kind, optional transform}, output {carrier, schema, facts}, optional resource_identity, pushdown {contract, operations}, contract_cid ``` For a keyed access path, `acquisition.correlation.cardinality` declares the **response cardinality** (`zero_or_one | zero_or_many | one | one_or_many`) per requested key. It is not an `output.facts` field or an authored join assertion. The correlation contract also names request fields, response fields, and response identity; [External SourceView joins](#external-joins) defines their use in external joins. Join cardinality assertions use the distinct vocabulary and meaning in [join](#join). Each SourceView's request contract MUST be a complete non-null checked object contract, including for views without correlation. Its fields may themselves be nullable; a nullable field still requires a value. A declared correlation uses a `search`, `fetch` or `follow` acquisition and refers to record fields of a Relation, Events or Vectors output. This field-based correlation grammar does not flatten a Graph's nodes or edges into a response record. Request and response field lists are nonempty, duplicate-free and have equal length. Positions pair in supplied order, and every pair resolves existing fields with compatible KeyComparable contracts. Their nullability, string extents and decimal precision/scale need not be identical; declaration compatibility does not bypass actual request-value constraints or the selected null-request policy. The declared response identity MUST be a nonempty ordered list of distinct existing response fields with non-null KeyComparable contracts. It may overlap the response key fields and need not equal an Events or Vectors intrinsic identity role. It is an acquisition response identity, not a replacement for that Carrier's semantic identity. Validation retains all supplied tuple orders and exact contract ownership without coercion. Non-null types alone do not prove identity uniqueness, response cardinality, completeness, ordering or successful request execution. The existing acquisition obligations still enforce those claims on actual responses.
