and - Run/apply receipt CIDs bind the exact published artifacts and outcomes, while a Result delivery receipt CID additionally binds one selected canonical byte representation ([Result delivery](protocols/artifacts.md#result-delivery)). The `actql-compiled-plan/0.1` compilation envelope is a closed canonical contract. It binds `compiler_version`, `aoa_ir_version`, `executable_plan_cid`, `program_definition_cid`, `program_semantics_cid`, `aoa_contract_cid`, and `aoa_logical_cid`; `compiled_plan_cid` hashes the complete body without only that self member. A Prepared Invocation refers to this envelope. Run admission checks the envelope against the exact Program Definition before execution, and later Receipt issuance derives its compiler, AoA, and semantic fields from the already admitted envelope. A publisher cannot supply replacement version or logical-identity strings. #### Local semantic identity and graph membership Unit namespace is the typed pair of stable authored Program id and node id. Unit Definition binds this namespace, the complete local body, used parameter and binding declarations, producer namespace/definition/export/port/type and correlation contracts, and incoming success/freshness declarations. It excludes parent revision CID, sibling bodies, unrelated exports, physical paths and array position. Renaming a node or changing its incoming dependency changes local meaning. Canonical extraction reuses a single-unit Program Definition and typed namespace encoding; ambiguous concatenation and duplicate artifact families are not permitted. The compiler MUST derive local parameter, binding, contract and review projections by the pinned law, including domain, guard, permission, scope and failure dependencies, not an optimizer's optional slice. Whole values and lock remain graph admission evidence. Local contract closure contains all interpreted schema, Mapping, Command, ModelTask, capacity, policy and numeric laws. Catalog membership, uniqueness of resolution and whole-lock authenticity remain checked; this is not automatic compatible-lock renewal. An exact Preview MUST bind Unit Definition, used effective values, local contract closure, exact admitted inputs/imports and observations, required issuer, order, completeness, policy/provenance, targets, payloads, guards, management-write recipe and resolved limits. Type equality alone cannot substitute a different producer receipt. Full ArtifactRef scope remains material. Global Program/lock/manifest CIDs, unrelated metadata, physical Run ids and the dispatch key itself are excluded, including indirect ancestry through Invocation, Result, receipt or parameter envelopes. Projected evidence has its own CID, never its parent's CID. The local_manifest_cid and semantic_outcome_cid reference roles resolve only to the registered semantic projections, not the Run-bound Manifest or full apply receipt. Their registered reference graph includes Result Artifact and local Invocation descendants. Required source-audit correspondence, signatures and membership are verified through separate projection attestations; retaining the entire Captured Run as evidence does not put its wrapper CID into Preview. Authenticated membership binds current graph revision/run, namespace, local definition and local artifacts outside their semantic hash preimages. Admission checks both local semantics and membership/producer authority. A same-shaped raw JSON value without evidence does not grant execution rights. Local review binds annotations actually reviewed for the unit and applicable shared root explanation; unrelated stage metadata and absolute UI positions are excluded. Browse-only context is distinct from signed review. Changing relevant explanation requires a new review; changing only node 3 leaves fixed node 1/2 templates unchanged. New graph launch still needs composition admission; reuse of earlier successful work requires an explicit recovery link, not silent replay of an old Resolution. The normative `actql-program-semantics/0.1` canonical envelope is: ```json { "version": "actql-program-semantics/0.1", "actql_version": "actql/0.1", "expression_contract_cid": "sha256:...", "parameters": {}, "parameter_references": [], "bindings": {}, "binding_references": [], "program_template": {} } ``` For the staged grammar, `program_template` is exactly `{stages: [{id, stage_semantics_cid, after, imports}, ...], exports}`. Descriptors retain stage order; after is `initial` for the first descriptor and the completed/accepted normalized law thereafter. Imports is a map from local input name to its explicit Result/receipt reference; exports is the root results map. No typed runtime artifacts or full source body are embedded here. Each stage_semantics_cid hashes the closed envelope `{version: "actql-stage-semantics/0.1", expression_contract_cid, parameters, parameter_references, bindings, binding_references, local_body}`. Local_body contains decoded inputs, steps, results and normalized effects (empty map when omitted), plus from only when authored; imported inputs remain explicit source references, not captured values. Parameters contains only declarations used by that stage, and parameter_references uses the common canonical reference enumeration relative to local_body. Each reference is exactly `{name, path, type}`, with the annotation-free declaration as type and an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer as path. Sort by path then name in canonical UTF-16 order, rejecting duplicate locations. Local paths start at local_body; root paths start at the decoded source document, not the descriptor array. Structural reference discovery never descends into opaque literal data. Bindings and binding_references apply the same used-only projection to opaque binding declarations, never their concrete runtime values. Empty maps/lists remain explicit. The registered envelope schemas admit source-body containers; the pinned structural grammar and semantic admission MUST validate their contents. References remain unbound. Stage id, after and every allowed annotation are excluded from local_body. The Stage Definition binds its stable stage ID and this semantics CID; Unit Definition adds the namespace and incoming contracts specified in [Local approval dependencies](#local-approval). Neither hashes the parent Program. Root parameters/references cover the entire Program and use source stage-relative pointers; they do not enter unrelated Unit Definitions. The Program template MUST use the stage descriptors defined above, not the complete source JSON as its template. Parameter declarations in both envelopes exclude annotations. The authority-bearing definition envelope is: ```json { "version": "actql-program-definition/0.1", "id": "crm.update_risk", "program_semantics_cid": "sha256:..." } ``` The Stage Definition MUST hash exactly the closed envelope `{version: "actql-stage-definition/0.1", id, stage_semantics_cid}`, where id is the normalized authored stage ID and stage_semantics_cid identifies that same stage's envelope above. There is no self-CID member in this preimage. The parent Program ID/CID, stage position, after, annotations and concrete values are not additional members. Changing the stage ID changes this definition even when its semantics are unchanged. This envelope is registered as schemas.stage_definition in the stage contract registry. It is not the Unit Definition: the typed Program/node namespace and incoming contracts remain separate local extraction requirements. Computing either source identity grants no execution authority. For an extracted stage, `used_parameter_declarations_cid` MUST hash exactly the canonical JSON map in that stage semantics envelope's `parameters` member. The map uses the same annotation-free declaration encoding and used-name selection already specified above; it is not the enclosing Program's parameter map, a map of concrete values, or a reference-occurrence list. An empty selection hashes `{}`. There is no additional version, namespace or self-CID wrapper. Defaults and constraints remain declaration semantics, while supplied values, binding origin and annotations do not enter this projection. Opaque Binding declarations remain in the separate stage semantics `bindings` member; this Parameter-only CID does not discharge their local dependency requirements. The existing stage-semantics `parameters` schema and semantic declaration validation govern the map; no additional artifact family is introduced. For a Unit extracted from a source stage, `local_body_cid` MUST identify that stage's complete `actql-stage-semantics/0.1` envelope, not only its `local_body` member and not its Stage Definition or the enclosing Program. This reuses the existing semantic envelope so that used Binding declarations, reference locations and the expression-contract pin remain part of the local meaning. The separately referenced used Parameter declaration map is the projection defined above, not an independently chosen declaration set. Unit namespace and incoming contracts remain separate members of the local dependency envelope; the stage semantics CID cannot replace either. This defines the `external:local-body` reference role for extracted source stages without adding another artifact family or weakening dependency/authority admission. Every self-CID is computed over the same envelope without its own CID field. Normalization journal and schema/capability/mapping evidence are not Program members. Evidence-dependent completion (for example expanding `drop` using a complete checked schema) appears in the journal and AoA plan, therefore changes Check Environment/Compiled Plan identity without changing Program identity. The separate AoA logical CID identifies only the main computation plan; each generated effect plan has its own AoA logical CID. The Run Receipt MUST bind all applicable identities, concrete input logical identities and evidence, the Result Manifest CID, and every published Result Artifact identity and completeness claim. It does not select a Result format or bind delivered bytes. Result byte hashes belong to the delivery receipt defined in [Result delivery](protocols/artifacts.md#result-delivery). ActQL semantic identities use that pinned AoA Kernel canonical JSON contract: Unicode string values are preserved and object member names are normalized at the boundaries specified in [Source representation](#source-representation), with the quoted Effect literal source-key exception defined there. Exact decoded keys in those payloads participate in Stage and Program semantic preimages before external target contracts are resolved. Composed and decomposed keys, or keys differing in CR/LF, therefore give different source identities even when later typed Object admission yields the same field. This does not make Program identity depend on a Mapping contract. Object keys are ordered by canonical code units, finite numbers use the AoA normalized number spelling, and negative zero is invalid. The ActQL CID is SHA-256 over the UTF-8 canonical serialization of its semantic envelope. Formatting, source key order, and comments do not affect this identity. A source-text hash MAY be retained separately as provenance. #### Local Result import interface For each declared Result import, the local `import_interface_cids` entry MUST identify the closed `schemas.result_import_interface` envelope registered in the stage contract: `{version: "actql-result-import-interface/0.1", input_name, producer_namespace: {program_id, node_id}, producer_unit_definition_cid, producer_result, value_contract_cid, availability: "stage_success", self_cid}`. Its self CID hashes canonical JSON of every member except `self_cid`. Names are source-normalized names. `input_name` is the consumer's local input name; `producer_result` is the producer's local Result name, not a root export alias or temporary dataflow name. The namespace and Unit Definition identify that exact producer. A Stage Definition, parent Program revision, local source handle or array index MUST NOT substitute for the producer Unit Definition. The `value_contract_cid` MUST resolve to the complete checked, nonnullable object value contract of the selected Result row schema, using the existing canonical value-contract encoding. This is a declared port contract, not a hash of rows, an observed Result artifact or a Host execution ceiling. Port ownership, field types and the producer definition MUST agree before constructing the interface; type equality alone does not prove producer identity. Unknown type evidence or an unresolved producer Unit Definition prevents construction. No observed value, Invocation, receipt, physical path or whole Catalog is added to this preimage. Selected contract semantics remain dependencies of the corresponding Unit; concrete policy and observation evidence remain execution admission material. Every declared Result import MUST have its own interface, including unused imports and distinct input names referring to the same Result. The consumer's interface list is ordered by normalized input name in UTF-16 code-unit order; source map enumeration order is not identity. A Result import requires successful producer computation and publication of that selected Result, independently of the consumer's predecessor-success gate. `after: accepted` does not waive data availability or required Ref availability. Zero rows retain the declared type. Receipt imports require their separate success-view and correlation contracts; they MUST NOT be encoded as this Result interface or silently omitted when their interpretation is unsupported. This static interface is neither proof of successful publication nor permission to activate the consumer. ##### Local contract selection and identity The compiler MUST select the exact transitive contract dependencies of the complete source-owned Unit inventory. Roots include the governing contracts of its declarations, operations, expressions, publication, imports and incoming gates, including domain, guard, permission, scope and failure rules. Selection does not perform liveness or branch pruning: unused declared inputs, authored no-ops and unselected expression branches remain in the inventory. A selected SourceView contributes its declared contract references, including the advertised read-mode contracts; unrelated Catalog members do not become local dependencies. Whole-Catalog membership, resolution uniqueness and whole-lock integrity are still validated outside this projection. Dependency traversal follows contract-bearing positions specified by each reached contract's registered governing grammar, not arbitrary CID-looking strings, business data or metadata. Unknown dependencies, wrong kinds, conflicting pins and unsupported dependency grammars prevent closure. Finite reference cycles retain every reached member once only where the governing grammar permits those cycles; cycle prohibitions and execution-prerequisite acyclicity remain unchanged. Existing contract identity rules determine the referenced CIDs without ad hoc metadata stripping or rehashing. A Unit Definition MUST distinguish policy/capacity interpretation contracts from concrete policy decisions, measured quantities and resolved limits. The former are semantic contract dependencies; the latter belong to their governing Plan or Invocation evidence and do not enter Unit Definition merely because Check consulted them. Authored guards remain part of the local body. This preserves the rule that changing Host policy values does not change Program Definition. The local contract closure CID MUST hash canonical JSON of the following whole envelope, registered as `schemas.local_contracts` in the stage contract registry. ```text {version:"actql-local-contracts/0.1", contracts:[contract_cid, ...]} ``` The array contains exactly the reached contract CIDs, each once, sorted in ascending UTF-16 code-unit order. Its entries have the canonical lowercase `sha256:` form. There is no self-CID field. The empty set uses the same versioned envelope with an empty array; it does not assert that a particular Unit has no governing laws. Source locations, traversal order, reference multiplicity and whole environment/Catalog identities are not part of this set preimage. Occurrence roles and repeated uses remain in the source-bound selection evidence and the Unit body/interfaces. Equal contract-set CIDs alone do not establish equal Unit Definitions or Invocations. Schema validation of a sorted CID set does not establish complete dependency selection or authority. ## Structural grammar (normative) The following JSON-model grammar is normative. `?` marks an optional member, `*` marks a string-keyed map, and `+` marks a non-empty string-keyed map. `|` separates alternatives; `&` merges members into one closed object. Object-form Input, Parameter, and Binding declarations additionally admit `meta?: Meta` as defined in [Authoring Context](#authoring-context). Their execution fields are defined in [Inputs and external contracts](#inputs); expressions in [Expressions and predicates](#expressions); operation bodies in [Operations](#operations); and Effect bodies in [Effect declarations](#effects). This alternative does not apply to other string fields or to the restricted EffectValue grammar below. Named productions resolve as follows: name classes and `InputOrStepName` in [Pipeline names and references](#pipeline-references)–[Field names and nested paths](#field-paths); `JsonValue`, `NonEmptyString`, and `PositiveSafeInteger` in [Source representation](#source-representation) and [Author guards, resolved limits, and Plan facts](#resolved-limits); Input, ParamDeclaration, and BindingDeclaration in [Local typed inputs](#local-inputs)–[Parameters and binding](#parameters); OperationName and OperationBody in [Operations](#operations); ResultDefinition in [Named Results and Effect declarations](#results-and-delivery); MappingRef, CommandContractRef, ResultField, TargetPrimaryKey, ScalarId, and Field in [Effect declarations](#effects). # Frontend r1: adopted query surfaces and machine Program input

Frontend r1 lowers adopted source forms to the common Program. It does not add an
execution engine, an alternative checker, or authority to acquire inputs or
apply Effects. The [adopted profile](../../spec/frontend/frontend-profile-r1.json)
separates accepted, restricted and rejected surfaces from implementation and
execution evidence. `supported` in the imported design means adoption, not
installed functionality. The [baseline and acceptance index](../../spec/frontend/README.md)
record delivery evidence separately.

The [standard-profile ledger](frontend-standard-profiles.md) selects semantic
references and distinguishes ActQL extensions. Common Program meaning must
align with adopted rules; historical implementation choices are not fixed
merely because an existing operation already represents them.

The accepted follow-on [SGA surface design](frontend-sga-surface.md) reuses
logical WITH bindings and existing Graph operations. It remains separate from
implemented syntax and public Host execution evidence.

## One Program and one operation vocabulary

JSON and YAML remain public machine inputs. The retired internal fixture
representation records the complete
closed Program envelope: metadata, IDs, parameters, opaque bindings, stages,
inputs, explicit steps, Results and Effects. Expression strings inside JSON
bodies retain the existing expression grammar. Object order is immaterial;
array order and explicit steps are preserved. Missing optional members and
explicitly empty permitted members are not conflated. An empty Effect map can
be represented by `EFFECTS {};` in the historical internal fixture language,
not the current public source language.

In historical fixtures only, `STEP` carries an ordinary JSON step, including its metadata and output name.
`OP` selects a name from the existing closed operation inventory. The minimum
structural `DATA` form chains only native operations, for example
`DATA x = OP values {...};` and `DATA y = FROM x |> OP filter {...};`.
These record historical productions, not current public examples. `WHERE`,
`SELECT`, query expressions, domain aliases and `MATCH` use the query frontend.
The entire old envelope is rejected by public source routing. Supported
SQL/Pipe and Graph query syntax follows query-text.md; the adopted target is
broader than implemented syntax. See [migration mapping](frontend-language-migration.md).

The internal fixture formatter reconstructs the admitted structure, including unused
steps and explicit no-ops. It does not optimize the Program or preserve comments
and whitespace. It does not use the metadata-stripped identity projection as
its source. Source text and semantic identity are distinct: trivia can change
source positions without changing the canonical Program.

## Bounded construction and origins

The frontend constructs the JSON-model source through a bounded builder and
ordinary admission. No public unchecked Program constructor is introduced.
Caller-supplied node counts, depths or byte counts are not trusted. Duplicate
keys, including normalization collisions, are rejected before they can be
collapsed into a map. Construction fails without publishing a partial Program
when a limit would be exceeded.

The existing `source_map.admit` traversal supplies owner-bound annotations and
ordinary `decode_core` admission. The builder retains origins through the
existing source-map mechanism rather than creating a second cursor identity
system. `stage_syntax` remains the Program issuer; `program_check.check_parsed`
and `check_parsed_with_evidence` remain the semantic checker entries.

Origins refer to original UTF-8 input before NFC and line-ending normalization.
Byte offsets, Unicode scalar columns and UTF-16 positions are distinct. Invalid
or out-of-range spans and annotations from another admitted owner are rejected.
Generated nodes retain their originating source range and generated-node role;
they do not claim an invented textual token range.

## Identity and execution boundaries

Canonical equivalence is compared under the same applicable contract pins.
Program IDs, Effect names, explicit steps and semantic array order remain
significant according to their existing contracts. A changed Grammar Manifest
can change dependent compilation identities; frontend equivalence is not a
promise that all Plan identities survive a grammar change.

The Grammar Manifest's structural-text fields bind the withdrawal grammar
and policy, separately from the existing Program source grammar and expression
contracts. They no longer authorize a structural parser or formatter. Its
pins, dependent artifacts and independent vectors change together with those
obligations; the Program schema remains unchanged.
All owned contracts remain on the initial 0.1 baseline.

That schema statement describes structural-text retirement, not a prohibition
on later coordinated semantic changes. The profile principle
`machine_program_semantics_preserved` requires lowering equivalence under the
applicable pins. It does not prohibit correcting the common model to match
an adopted standard. Such corrections update affected laws, schemas, pins,
canonical identities and independent vectors together.

Pure checking performs no provider I/O. Execution uses the normal Host and
existing checked owners, retaining Effect declarations and acquisition
boundaries. Source translation does not prove backend support for an operation.
The 72-operation language inventory and Local execution-path accounting count
different things.

The lightweight transport SDK does not depend on the parser or Core. Existing
`aql`, `start`, `attach` and Result behavior stays intact. Historical structural tests are fixture-tool tests; they cannot submit old
text to the public Host. Public machine-input execution and new source
execution are distinct acceptance claims.
No second Run API, SQL engine, retry mechanism or Effect scheduler is needed.

## Query profiles and remaining adoption work

The statement-level `|> RESULT name` extension refers to the complete current
Relation through ordinary named step producers and Stage/Program Results. A
continuing Pipe consumes the same carrier, while each named Result retains its
own visible schema, duplicates and existing evidence at that point. A terminal
RESULT supplies the configured primary output without a duplicate export.
When immutable range snapshots occupy private slots, a separate ordinary
projection exposes current columns and the continuing Pipe resumes the full
producer. This preserves valid old-value references without publishing helper
slots. No additional source acquisition or execution owner is introduced.

RESULT declarations are forbidden inside pure CTE/derived-query bodies and set
operands. A top-level pipeline may consume their evaluated Relation and retain
it. Graph pattern output needs an explicit Relation projection; its occurrence
slots are not an implicit public schema. Adopted statement sequencing,
`RESULT(name)` source references and BRANCH integration remain distinct work.

Query, Pipe and limited graph patterns lower into the same Program. The
profile registry records their
preconditions and rejection reasons. Restricted syntax is not expanded by
guessing schema, inserting casts, hiding acquisition, approximating computation,
or treating a runtime capability declaration as execution evidence.

Known gaps in the imported acceptance matrix are explicit fixture requirements
in the registry. They remain work to do; an empty evidence array is never a pass.

### Quoted String profile

The selected lexical reference is
[GoogleSQL lexical structure at the pinned reference revision](https://github.com/google/googlesql/blob/d82db99a923a46571f543a13899dc791a7b6f743/docs/lexical.md#string-and-bytes-literals).
Query strings lower to ordinary String literals. Their decoded scalar values
are retained by the common value, canonical identity and serialization owners;
the Frontend does not introduce an alternative String representation.

| Reference form | Frontend and common meaning | Coverage boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single/double quoted String | The same bounded decoder and String expression; either quote may contain the other quote | Raw CR/LF is invalid in these plain forms |
| Standard simple, octal, hex and Unicode escapes | Decode once to the exact Unicode scalar sequence | Reject malformed escapes, surrogate values and values above U+10FFFF |
| Backtick identifier | Same non-raw scalar escape decoder as String; decoded names enter ordinary name resolution | Nonempty; physical CR/CRLF decodes to LF; common authored-name constraints still apply; no raw/triple/chunk concatenation |
| Triple single/double quoted String | Ordinary String after source newline/escape decoding | Three matching unescaped quotes terminate the chunk; physical newlines are permitted |
| Raw String | Preserve each backslash and following scalar in an ordinary String | Prefix applies only to its immediate chunk; odd trailing backslash and plain-form physical newlines reject |
| Adjacent String chunks | Concatenate decoded values into one String expression, retaining the original source range | Whitespace/comment separation is required; identifiers and String/bytes mixtures do not concatenate |
| Bytes literal | Requires the reference's distinct bytes meaning | Not yet implemented; never stringify bytes silently |
| Graph label membership | The admitted Graph owns labels independently of ordinary properties | The retired query-local LABELS annotation is rejected |

Independent fixtures compare decoded values and ordinary Programs, including
CR/LF/CRLF, composed/decomposed Unicode and backslash followed by `n`. The
packed source fixtures require rows, declaration-order contracts and UTF-8
extents through the same Local/HTTP Result boundary. Listed fixture obligations
do not by themselves establish execution success.

## Shared query vocabulary and scope

### Relational query bodies

The selected [GoogleSQL Pipe reference](https://github.com/google/googlesql/blob/d82db99a923a46571f543a13899dc791a7b6f743/docs/pipe-syntax.md)
allows standard and Pipe syntax to be mixed, including different syntax in a
subquery and its parent. A named FROM/JOIN subquery and a CTE therefore share
the relational-body parser, original source positions and query resource
budgets. SELECT heads retain their optional ORDER BY/LIMIT; FROM heads and
SELECT heads can both use the existing pure relational Pipe operators.

Both contexts lower through the existing producer/Stage Result boundary. A
parent reads the body's output columns and range variable, not the body's
hidden source columns or displaced aliases. Parsing does not query a Catalog,
copy a source, authorize acquisition or introduce another execution engine.

The same query-expression parser covers parenthesized roots, nested
non-recursive WITH bodies and set-operation bodies. A Pipe tail after a
parenthesized or combined set producer operates on its retained output; it
does not expand that producer into another acquisition. Nested CTE declarations
retain lexical visibility and are bound after their bodies, so an inner
declaration can read an already-visible outer CTE before shadowing its name.
CTE aliases are case-insensitive even when quoted, independently of the
Source View identifier profile. Hidden body columns and out-of-scope CTEs are
not made visible by internal producer names.

An ORDER BY expression following a set is resolved only against the combined
output fields, using its first operand's output names. Existing common
expressions derive any sort-only slot once; repeated equivalent terms reuse
it. Ordinary sort and a final projection preserve the declared output without
publishing hidden sort fields. Operand range variables, non-output columns
and aliases unique to a later operand remain out of scope. This follows the
selected [GoogleSQL ORDER BY reference](https://github.com/google/googlesql/blob/d82db99a923a46571f543a13899dc791a7b6f743/docs/query-syntax.md#order_by_clause)
and its [independent analyzer cases](https://github.com/google/googlesql/blob/d82db99a923a46571f543a13899dc791a7b6f743/googlesql/analyzer/testdata/orderby.test).

This does not claim every query composition is implemented. Positional numeric
ORDER BY terms remain an implementation gap and are not interpreted as
constant sort keys. INFER/Graph-query placement retains its separate boundary;
this relational unit does not make those queries executable within a CTE or
derived table.

SQL and Pipe use the adopted GoogleSQL vocabulary and one query expression
representation before lowering to existing Program expressions and operations.
They do not roundtrip generated expression strings through the legacy parser.
The source remains bounded and carries original byte positions into admission.
See [semantic decision criteria](semantic-decisions.md#vocabulary-across-representations).

SELECT aliases take precedence over input names in GROUP BY, HAVING and final
ORDER BY, subject to ambiguity, grouping and clause-visibility checks. WHERE and
the same SELECT list cannot refer to newly introduced SELECT aliases. Qualified
references retain their source binding; qualification does not authorize an
ungrouped reference after aggregation. Analytic arguments and OVER use their
own context-dependent scopes, not a copy of final ORDER BY's scope.

Ordinary SELECT may order by visible, unprojected source expressions. DISTINCT
orders only by expressions legally resolved from its projected output, including
selected-expression and alias references. Hidden sort fields never participate
in DISTINCT equality or leak into Results. Alias resolution reuses the relevant
computed slot and does not duplicate evaluation or change failure/resource
accounting. Proof-only tie completion remains the existing compiler's concern.

These name-resolution rules follow [GoogleSQL query syntax](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax)
and [window function calls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/window-function-calls).
The selected ActQL profile rejects unsupported forms explicitly. NULL,
numeric and failure behavior must be compared with the selected reference;
an intentional difference needs a named profile or recorded rationale. Explicit
acquisition and authority boundaries remain common execution obligations.

| Reference term | Frontend representation | Existing semantic representation | Difference or boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SELECT list | Ordered projection expressions | derive and select | Preserve evaluation once and output order; duplicate output names rejected |
| Range variable / SELECT alias | Separate scope bindings | Resolved field slots | Pipe SET/DROP/RENAME retain prior range slots; Pipe AS replaces all old ranges with the current row; no helper egress |
| WHERE / HAVING | Pre-/post-aggregate predicate | filter plus existing expression tree | Three-valued logic and common demand/failure contracts; do not infer mandatory short-circuiting or evaluation order from GoogleSQL AND/OR |
| GROUP BY / aggregate call | Group keys and aggregate expressions | group | Not an analytic partition; canonical aggregate failure order retained |
| Analytic partition / window frame | OVER partition, order and ROWS frame | analytic | Not TEA event-time windows; only adopted signatures/frames |
| Final ORDER BY | Query output ordering | sort | Explicit ASC NULLS FIRST / DESC NULLS LAST; proof-driven tie completion |
| INNER / LEFT / FULL / CROSS JOIN | Scoped relation join and equality keys; USING exposes a merged unqualified key | join / cross_join plus checked output bound; FULL key through derive/coalesce | FULL needs stable row identity; no implicit representative row or key |
| UNION / INTERSECT / EXCEPT | Positional or exact BY NAME alignment | projection plus append/distinct/row-set | No implicit type promotion or missing-column padding |
| Nonrecursive CTE | SELECT or relational Pipe body; SELECT or Pipe head after WITH | Shared Stage captured input and step references | No reacquisition per reference; no recursive CTE |
| FROM subquery | Named noncorrelated query source | Checked Stage Result with a source alias | No correlated reference or independent runtime; nested source stages preserve ordinary admission |
| Parameter | Named query parameter | Existing parameter expression | @name binds without ASCII case to the exact admitted declaration name; legacy machine $name remains unchanged |
| CONCAT / ACTQL.CONCAT | Closed function mapping | concat_strict / concat | Strict STRING NULL propagation versus explicit legacy null-skipping |

The table defines obligations, not implementation status. Delivery evidence
records unimplemented features separately from intentional incompatibilities.


### Query parameter name binding

The selected GoogleSQL source rule resolves named parameters without ASCII case,
including decoded backtick names. The pinned resolver
[`ResolveParameterExpr`](https://github.com/google/googlesql/blob/d82db99a923a46571f543a13899dc791a7b6f743/googlesql/analyzer/resolver_expr.cc#L2418)
uses `AsciiStrToLower` before looking up named query parameters. The Frontend
binds that namespace to the exact name of an admitted Program declaration.
For example, declaration `p` and source `SELECT @P AS value` emit `$param: "p"`;
declaration `P` emits `$param: "P"` even when the source spells `@p`.

This is source name resolution, not a change to machine Parameter identity,
types, defaults, bound values, nullability, or permissions. Value dictionaries
still use the exact admitted declaration names. Two declarations whose names
collide under ASCII case folding reject the source compile context; an unknown
name remains unknown for ordinary checking. No declaration or value is inferred
from the source text.

One bounded declaration-name index supplies expression lowering, whole-operation
parameter slots, and expression type probes such as nullable ARRAY/STRUCT
UNNEST. Source expression reuse and analytic window sharing compare names in
that same namespace; case variants must not cause SELECT reevaluation or
separate equivalent window computations. Literal data and non-ASCII characters
are not changed by ASCII lookup. Common checker and execution owners retain
all missing-value, extra-value, type, domain and resource admission rules.
